findings.highlight: It’s still nine in the morning
findings.evidenceJa: まだ午前九時の中頃だというのに
findings.governingReading: even though it is only around half past nine in the morning
findings.explanation: The English broadens a mid-hour time anchor to the entire nine o’clock hour.

findings.highlight: the area in front of the station
findings.evidenceJa: 駅前のパーク
findings.governingReading: the park or plaza in front of the station
findings.explanation: A named kind of public space is reduced to a generic area, weakening Fuyuki’s local geography.

findings.highlight: Miyama City
findings.evidenceJa: 深山町
findings.governingReading: Miyama-chō or Miyama Town
findings.explanation: The district name is recast as a city and changes the settlement hierarchy within Fuyuki.

findings.highlight: people passing by are looking at her curiously
findings.evidenceJa: 通り過ぎていく連中はそろってセイバーを物珍しげに眺めていく
findings.governingReading: everyone passing by looks at Saber as an unusual sight
findings.explanation: The English omits that the reaction is uniform, which explains the relentlessness of Saber’s discomfort.

findings.highlight: we should at least do whatever we want today
findings.evidenceJa: 今日ぐらいは好きなコトをしてもいいだろ
findings.governingReading: today of all days, Saber may do what she likes
findings.explanation: Shirou’s invitation for Saber to choose is changed into a joint license for both of them.

findings.highlight: The future looks bad
findings.evidenceJa: 前途多難だ
findings.governingReading: there will be plenty of difficulties ahead
findings.explanation: A comic judgment about the outing’s difficult prospects becomes a broad pessimistic forecast.

findings.highlight: Let’s just go to random stores.
findings.evidenceJa: 手当たり次第に店をハシゴしよう
findings.governingReading: Let us hop from one shop to the next indiscriminately
findings.explanation: The repeated shop-to-shop movement disappears and indiscriminate selection becomes randomness.

findings.highlight: started to complain about something
findings.evidenceJa: こう[ruby text=つらつら char=2]連々と文句を言いだす
findings.governingReading: starts reeling off complaints at length like this
findings.explanation: The reading and sustained flow of Saber’s lecture are reduced to an unspecified single complaint.

findings.highlight: your lack of planning
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方の見積もりの甘さ
findings.governingReading: the softness or overoptimism of your estimates
findings.explanation: Saber criticizes Shirou’s habit of underestimating costs; the English changes this to having no plan at all.

findings.highlight: I won’t change my mind no matter what.
findings.evidenceJa: 絶対だ
findings.governingReading: It is absolute.
findings.explanation: The short final hammer blow of Shirou’s resolve is omitted after the preceding proposition.

findings.highlight: I look at Saber.
findings.evidenceJa: 正面からセイバーを見据える
findings.governingReading: He fixes Saber with a direct, unwavering look.
findings.explanation: The force and confrontational directness of his gaze disappear.

findings.highlight: I won’t have to worry about making you unhappy if you do so.
findings.evidenceJa: その方がお互い気兼ねしなくて済む
findings.governingReading: That way neither of them will need to hold back around the other.
findings.explanation: Mutual freedom from reserve becomes Shirou’s one-sided anxiety about upsetting Saber.

findings.highlight: averts her gaze and runs out of words
findings.evidenceJa: 視線を泳がせて言葉を濁す
findings.governingReading: her gaze wanders and she equivocates
findings.explanation: Saber’s uncharacteristic evasiveness becomes a simple inability to continue speaking.

findings.highlight: follow me
findings.evidenceJa: はぐれないように付いてこい
findings.governingReading: follow him so she does not get separated in the crowd
findings.explanation: The practical reason for maintaining contact while running through the crowd disappears.

findings.highlight: I just have to take her to every possible place I can think of.
findings.evidenceJa: あとは思いつくかぎりのエスコートをするだけだ
findings.governingReading: All that remains is to escort her as well as he can think how.
findings.explanation: The social role and conduct of escorting Saber are changed into maximizing the number of destinations.

findings.highlight: She must have accepted it as Saber finally stops complaining and follows me quietly.
findings.evidenceJa: 観念したのか、なにやら色々と文句を言っていたセイバーも大人しくなってくれた
findings.governingReading: Perhaps resigned to it, Saber quiets down after voicing various complaints.
findings.explanation: A tentative explanation is fused to the result with a malformed as-clause, obscuring both the uncertainty and sequence.

findings.highlight: surprise her
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの度肝を抜いてやろう
findings.governingReading: knock Saber’s socks off or astonish her
findings.explanation: Shirou’s exaggerated goal of utterly flooring Saber is weakened to ordinary surprise.

findings.highlight: We also went to an antique store
findings.evidenceJa: 趣味で骨董品屋に立ち寄ったのはご愛敬だし
findings.governingReading: His self-indulgent stop at an antique shop can be forgiven as a charming lapse.
findings.explanation: The English lists the stop without admitting it served Shirou’s own hobby or preserving his comic plea for indulgence.

findings.highlight: But I don’t think this is what people would call a date.
findings.evidenceJa: これは間違っても世間一般でいうデートじゃないと思う
findings.governingReading: He thinks this cannot possibly be what people ordinarily call a date.
findings.explanation: A stray alternative But remains before the sentence and introduces an unsupported contrast marker.

findings.highlight: She gives no reaction
findings.evidenceJa: お世辞にも楽しんでいた、と説明するのは憚られるぐらいの無反応ぶり
findings.governingReading: Her lack of reaction is such that he hesitates to claim, even flatteringly, that she enjoyed herself.
findings.explanation: The English removes Shirou’s qualified interpretive judgment and leaves only a bare description.

findings.highlight: I became desperate to make her happy at the next place
findings.evidenceJa: 次こそは次こそはと躍起になる
findings.governingReading: At each failure he becomes frantic that the next place will be the one.
findings.explanation: The repeated renewal of his resolve across successive stops is collapsed into one future attempt.

findings.highlight: I complain
findings.evidenceJa: 思わずごちた
findings.governingReading: He involuntarily mutters to himself.
findings.explanation: A quiet involuntary utterance becomes an explicit complaint.

findings.highlight: the restaurant by the river
findings.evidenceJa: 川沿いの喫茶店
findings.governingReading: the café by the river
findings.explanation: The establishment’s category changes from a café or coffee shop to a restaurant.

findings.highlight: I trusted her and chose this place
findings.evidenceJa: それに従って店を選んだ
findings.governingReading: He followed that advice in choosing the establishment.
findings.explanation: Compliance with a specific recommendation becomes a broader statement of personal trust in Rin.

findings.highlight: it would be so fastidious
findings.evidenceJa: こんな気難しそうな店
findings.governingReading: such a forbidding or exacting-looking establishment
findings.explanation: The adjective is attached as an unnatural personality judgment about the place rather than its intimidating atmosphere.

findings.highlight: today has been really exhausting
findings.evidenceJa: 今日はひどく緊張したので
findings.governingReading: because she has been terribly tense today
findings.explanation: Saber identifies sustained tension as the cause of unusual fatigue; the English replaces that cause with a generally exhausting day.

findings.highlight: The small gurgling sound was fortunately small enough that only I could hear.
findings.evidenceJa: きゅう、という小さな音は、幸い俺の耳にしか届かなかったようだ
findings.governingReading: Fortunately, the small kyuu sound seems to have reached only Shirou’s ears.
findings.explanation: The English asserts the audience and invents low volume as its cause, removing Shirou’s ようだ uncertainty.

findings.highlight: Oh. …Oh. If she was hungry, she could’ve just told me.
findings.evidenceJa: なんだ、お腹が減ってたんなら減ってたって言えばいいのに
findings.governingReading: Oh—if she was hungry, she could simply have said so.
findings.explanation: Two competing realizations are printed in succession, visibly interrupting the comic timing.

findings.highlight: it would be helpful for us to have lunch quickly
findings.evidenceJa: 昼食は早めにしてもらえると助かる
findings.governingReading: she would appreciate having lunch sooner rather than later
findings.explanation: Saber asks to advance the meal; the English can mean eating it rapidly instead.

findings.highlight: anything physical is not good
findings.evidenceJa: 体を動かす遊びはあまりよろしくない
findings.governingReading: physically active games are not a very good choice
findings.explanation: A conclusion about active recreation on the date is generalized to anything physical.

findings.highlight: Saber got angry
findings.evidenceJa: むーっとヘソを曲げてしまった
findings.governingReading: Saber went into a pout or sulk
findings.explanation: Her childish, comic displeasure at attracting attention becomes generic anger.

findings.highlight: English tea
findings.evidenceJa: 紅茶
findings.governingReading: black tea or tea
findings.explanation: The English repeatedly specifies English tea although the source only names tea.

findings.highlight: even if we did, it’s all instant tea-bags
findings.evidenceJa: 出したところでインスタントだ
findings.governingReading: when served at home, even then it is instant tea
findings.explanation: The translation invents tea bags as the form of the instant tea.

findings.highlight: She drinks her tea, sitting up straight
findings.evidenceJa: 凛とした姿勢でティーカップを口に運ぶ
findings.governingReading: With dignified composure, she raises the teacup to her lips.
findings.explanation: Saber’s poised bearing and precise action are reduced to spinal posture and generic drinking.

findings.highlight: I also know her attitude after she lets go of her sword.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が知っているのは、剣を手にした後の彼女でしかない
findings.governingReading: The only Saber he has known is her after she took the sword in hand.
findings.explanation: The English reverses taking up the sword into letting it go and changes an exclusivity claim into additional knowledge.

findings.highlight: This scene looks natural rather than new because this is her true nature.
findings.evidenceJa: この光景が新鮮に映らず、自然に感じられるのは、それが彼女の本質だからだろう
findings.governingReading: He supposes the scene feels natural because it is her essential nature.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s interpretive だろう is promoted into a factual declaration about Saber’s true nature.

findings.highlight: it’s abnormal for her to hold a sword at all
findings.evidenceJa: むしろ剣を持っている方が、この少女には異常な事なのかもしれない
findings.governingReading: Perhaps it is instead the act of holding a sword that is abnormal for this girl.
findings.explanation: A possibility framed through Shirou’s reflection becomes an unqualified absolute judgment.

findings.highlight: Saber is resting, not holding a sword.
findings.evidenceJa: 剣を持たず、緊張を解いて体を休めるセイバー
findings.governingReading: Saber rests her body without a sword, her tension released.
findings.explanation: The relaxation that distinguishes this scene from her habitual battle readiness disappears.

findings.highlight: This calm scene is the way she should be.
findings.evidenceJa: その穏やかな風景こそ、彼女がいるべき場所なんだから
findings.governingReading: This peaceful scene is precisely where she ought to be.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s strong conclusion about the place or state Saber belongs in becomes a judgment about how she should behave.
